quotes.text: Do not extinguish the passage, but do not feed a furnace that warms only its master.
"No," said Liora. "Narrow it to a testing stream. If fairness returns, open wide at once.
generosity answers generosity; repeated selfishness earns caution; renewed fairness restores confidence.
The Fox called this proof of greed and urged her to turn away.
Yet when conduct repeats, let memory guard the lamp.
Nema then carved a fourth law beneath the reeds
Generous travelers received broad gates; uncertain ones received cautious openings; and renewed fairness widened every road again.
Mist changes measures, not intentions.
answer risk with slightly more than half when the whole hand was opened
They call it the Covenant: trust first, reward courage, forgive the mist.
"Silence reveals caution, not always character," Liora answered.

note: Liora's Covenant grows reeds (Memory, Mercy, Measure); repeat takers get one ember, reopening immediately on fairness.

quotes.text: Against repeated silence, close the gate for a season. When seasons change, offer a cup, not the spring.
greed would narrow the next load without sealing the crossing forever
begin bravely, reward fairness, punish betrayal calmly, and leave a path back toward light.
"Cut the rope," cried the crow. "A silent shore deserves abandonment."
Courage need not be reckless, and punishment need not be eternal.
The river then carved a fifth law beneath Oar and Ledger
"Do not mistake a ripple for a betrayal."
When another risks much, return more than bare recovery.

note: Aster's numbered winter laws: send nothing for a season after repeated silence, then a small cup; crow's abandonment rejected.

quotes.text: So she sent no water across the valley.
Instead, she kept all three.
"No," said the Lake. "You learned fear, then became what you feared. That stranger risked despite past wounds. You hoarded despite preaching wisdom."
Knowledge had become not a bridge to action, but a beautiful shelter from it.
"You had your chance," replied the Builder. "Trust is not infinite.
She stood alone at the empty Fountain, wondering what use is wisdom that no one practices.
Someone must dare to pour the first cup, even after disappointment, or the wells serve no one.
And fear wearing the mask of wisdom is still just fear.
The circle remained unbroken. Eight mirrors, eight closed hands, eight perfect justifications.

note: Recurring keepers/travelers who preach trust but keep everything; stories indict the hypocrisy. R4 Builder's exclusion of a thief is endorsed.

quotes.text: close your hand when a neighbor repeatedly closes theirs. But leave the gate of redemption unlocked.
Yet when closed hands become a habit, narrow the crossing until proof of change appears.
Still, the bridge remained standing, ready to widen when Var risked his own flame or returned another’s abundance with justice.
Nhal pointed at Orin’s empty voyages. “Send nothing,” he urged.
Forgive isolated darkness and numbers blurred by fog, but narrow the bridge when selfishness repeats.
Trust became a bridge: widened by reciprocity, narrowed by selfishness, and never ruled by fear alone.
“Measure not a single splash. Remember the pattern of the tide.”
“Do not call every closed palm wicked,” it warned. “Fear may have been taught by an earlier betrayal
She trusted evidence, not certainty, knowing that abundance requires someone to move first.

note: Luma reads each partner's record; whisperer Nhal tempts both ways; habitual takers get a closed purse with the bridge left standing.

quotes.text: Tavek, before he kept the ferry, was a hoarder. The first time the river Anshu asked a gift of him, he gave nothing
Tavek kept the ferry forty years, but the elders do not hide his second sin.
kept all nine. He told himself the fog was to blame. He told himself she would not know.
Punish by shrinking, never by vanishing.
Trim, do not extinguish — send less, but never nothing, for nothing is the only sentence the river cannot revise.
And on the morning the sealed door opens — load full before you have finished feeling surprised
Forgive the fog twice. The third time, trim — gently, and name no one a thief.
Grow what returns. Shrink what does not. But never let the number reach zero and stay there —
The Eleventh Post: The Ledger and the Lamp
Do not read malice in the water's stutter.
Someone must untie first, and the untying costs little when it is small.
And when they load true, overpay. Return more than half.

note: Ferryman Tavek's past hoarding told as confessed sins (R2-R3); later carvings: shrink, never vanish, keep a lamp lit.

quotes.text: proven greed narrows the bridge until changed deeds reopen it
close them against demonstrated greed, and leave every gate capable of reopening.
The Jackal of Suspicion whispered, “Judge every empty gate alike.”
after betrayal, waits for proof before blooming again.
So the clans added a fourth law to their ancient covenant
neither accused the other; they judged patterns, not a single wave.
withholding one’s own purse differs from seizing another’s trust.

note: Liora/Sera distinguish absent gifts from exploitation; proven greed narrows the bridge until conduct changes.

quotes.text: the Gate of Equal Eyes watched not the sum but the honesty behind it; the Gate of Mercy welcomed restraint to spare the other
The people learned to name their aim aloud before stepping onto the Bridge, to name their fear, to name what they could spare.

note: Bridge/Gates template (Equal Eyes, Mercy, Memory) repeated; vague balance plus naming intent aloud; no sanction rule.
